New vignettes, vignette("ordination") vignette("stat_tests"), walk , README vignette("ecodive") give overview everything package . package title now “Parallel Memory-Efficient Ecological Diversity Analysis”. New plot() methods draw ecodive’s results base graphics (‘graphics’ ‘grDevices’, R 3.6.0 ), taking titles, axis labels, subtitles legends result holds, computing nothing new: Ordinations (pcoa(), pca(), dbrda(), nmds(), procrustes(), …) draw two axes, labelled share variance, method’s fit subtitle (stress, R-squared, …). plot(ord, "Species", iris) colours samples column metadata, legend, groups data tests; supervised ordinations colour groups. Loadings, constraint arrows, centroids Procrustes rotation’s target drawn top. plot(envfit(...), add = TRUE) adds fitted variables ordination plot. Permutation tests show permutation distribution statistic, observed value marked; mrpp() permdisp() show group’s within-group distance dispersion, procrustes_test() Procrustes fit (type = "null" distribution). simper() gives dot chart taxa contribute pair’s dissimilarity, dirmult_ttest() volcano, effect, MA forest plot (see ), ancom() dot chart W, varpart() Venn diagram fractions (two four sets), forward_select() adjusted R-squared step, bioenv() best correlation number variables. Distance matrices give heatmap, samples’ order sorted groups, colour key: beta_div() every metric function, vlr(), rho_p() phi_s() (features), rpca()’s dm. now class c("ecodive_dist", "dist"), plot() knows ; base R plot() method dist objects, every function dist objects works . Code checks identical(class(d), "dist") class(d) == "dist" use inherits(d, "dist") instead. ancombc() ancombc2() give volcano, effect, MA forest plot one covariate’s log fold changes, ancombc_pairwise() ancombc_dunnett() heatmap log fold change feature comparison, ancombc_global() ancombc_trend() dot chart statistics. Every function returns distance matrix, beta_div() 38 metric functions, vlr(), rho_p() phi_s(), takes clust, cluster samples returning : one stats::hclust()’s linkage methods ("average", "complete", "single", "ward.D", "ward.D2", "mcquitty", "median", "centroid"), "pcoa" order along first axis pcoa(). Clustering reorders samples result, labels (unnamed samples labelled input positions); matrix’s order attribute gives one’s position input. ecodive’s ordinations tests put samples back input order analysing , metadata lines whether matched name position; packages, reorder metadata attr(d, "order"). clust = NULL, default, leaves matrix , plot() clusters average linkage heatmap; clust = FALSE (kept "none") keeps input order plot . New partition beta diversity (Baselga 2010, 2012, 2013, 2017), ‘betapart’ computes : Eight new beta metrics, run beta_div() like : sorensen_turnover() (Simpson dissimilarity, "betasim"), sorensen_nestedness(), jaccard_turnover() jaccard_nestedness() presence/absence; bray_balanced(), bray_gradient(), soergel_balanced() soergel_gradient() (Ruzicka components) abundances, ported ‘abdiv’ (MIT). pair components adds sorensen(), jaccard(), bray() soergel(). New beta_partition() returns three distance matrices family (index = "sorensen", "jaccard", "bray" "ruzicka") one pass pairs, betapart::beta.pair() beta.pair.abund(); plot() draws pair’s turnover nestedness. New beta_partition_multi() gives multiple-site values whole set samples, beta.multi() beta.multi.abund(), n_sites, n_draws random subsets many samples (beta.sample(), ecodive’s random numbers: seed); plot() draws draws’ densities. beta_div(x, "Bray-Curtis") (alias "braycurtis", "bc") still selects bray() now metric names begin “Bray-Curtis”. Distance matrices, ordinations, permutation tests envfit() title, plot() uses unless given main (?ecodive_display): method’s name, title result computed , “Principal Coordinates Analysis Bray-Curtis Dissimilarity”. kept one attribute, display, list ecodive’s plot() print(), beside distance matrix’s clust; set attr(x, "display")$title retitle result. distance matrix’s method attribute metric’s ID ("bray"), stats::dist() sets . Results don’t record arguments earlier steps made . Arithmetic distance matrix (sqrt(d)) drops title method, since longer describe values. vlr(), rho_p() phi_s() longer return denominator pseudocount attributes. Ordinations, distance matrices ecodive’s data frames (ancom(), ancombc(), ancombc2() post-hoc tests, dirmult_ttest(), simper(), bioenv() envfit()) print preview, manner tibble package, rather every value (?print_ecodive): header object’s kind, size title; first 10 rows (20), column’s type; columns fit console; footer counting left naming attributes. distance matrix shows top-left corner lower triangle. print(x, n = Inf) shows every row, .data.frame(), .matrix() unclass() give plain object. Every function’s examples print result. New pcoa() runs principal coordinates analysis (classical multidimensional scaling) dist object, beta_div(). gives coordinates eigenvalues cmdscale(), ape::pcoa(), vegan::wcmdscale() (axis’s sign), computes first axes (n_axes = 3 default), parallel C, without forming n--n matrix. results identical number cpus. correction = "lingoes" "cailliez" adds smallest constant squared distances, distances, leaves negative eigenvalue, giving constants, eigenvalues coordinates ape::pcoa(), vegan::wcmdscale(add = ) cmdscale(add = TRUE), without n--n (2n--2n) matrix: 2,000 samples, "cailliez" takes 20 seconds cmdscale(add = TRUE) takes 2 minutes. Every result correction constant attributes. New pcoa_biplot() projects features table (taxa counts, environmental variables) onto axes pcoa() result, drawing arrows PCoA plot. computes scores scikit-bio’s pcoa_biplot(), parallel C, keeps sparse tables sparse, takes every table type norm pca() . envfit() gives directions permutation tests. Every ordination function takes number axes return n_axes (3 default methods whose axes eigenvalues: pcoa(), pca(), rpca(), dbrda(), capscale() isomap(); 2 mds(), nmds(), tsne() umap()). name says counts; k, cmdscale() vegan call , often means number neighbours methods. New dist_ord() runs distance-based ordination method name, beta_div() beta diversity metrics dist_test() statistical tests, method’s arguments: dist_ord(dm, "nmds") nmds(dm). list_dist_ords() match_dist_ord() list look methods. count_ord(), list_count_ords() match_count_ord(), methods take count table rather distances, pca(), rda(), cca(), ca(), lda(), plsda(), oplsda(), rpca() rpca_phylo(): count_ord(counts, "pca") pca(counts). wrapper points given ’s method, dist_test() given test. Every ordination method returns kind result: sample--axis matrix (class "ecodive_ord", prints attributes’ names rather contents) whose attributes start method, eig, prop. Every method rejects negative distances (beyond rounding error), seed can given dist_ord(). New nmds() runs non-metric multidimensional scaling SMACOF algorithm scikit-learn’s non-metric MDS(), ported parallel C. starts PCoA solution n_starts random configurations, keeps one lowest Kruskal stress-1, centers , rotates principal axes, scales distances. Tied distances use Kruskal’s primary approach (vegan::metaMDS()), scikit-learn’s secondary one ties = "secondary". distances sorted shared starts; nothing n--n formed. start runs max_iters iterations, stops stress improves less tol. Random starts come seed argument, results identical number cpus. result’s attributes stress, converged, n_iters, n_starts, best_start, n_best, ties. New mds() runs metric multidimensional scaling SMACOF algorithm scikit-learn’s metric MDS(), fitting distances rather ranks. shares nmds()’s engine, starts, arguments (without ties) result format, limit number samples. dist_ord(dm, "mds") "metric MDS" select ; "classical MDS", "pco" "cmdscale" select pcoa(). New isomap() runs Isomap (isometric feature mapping) ordination: links sample n_neighbors nearest neighbors (within radius), replaces distance shortest path graph, runs pcoa() geodesic distances, keeps long ecological gradients straight pcoa() bends arch. C port scikit-learn’s Isomap(metric = "precomputed"), gives geodesic distances embedding rounding, breaks ties sample order, joins disconnected neighbor graphs closest samples, warning (vegan::isomap() stops instead; note k number neighbors, isomap()’s n_axes number axes). neighbor shortest-path searches run parallel without n--n matrix, results identical number cpus. New tsne() runs t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) dist object, port scikit-learn’s TSNE parallel C. gradient = "auto" uses exact gradient 500 samples (3 dimensions) Barnes-Hut approximation (quadtree 2 dimensions, octree 3) . finds nearest neighbors exactly distances never forms n--n matrix. starts PCoA solution default, sets learning rate scikit-learn’s rule (learning_rate = "auto"), stops early layout stops improving (max_iters iterations; number run n_iters attribute), lowers perplexity small datasets. layouts match scikit-learn’s Rtsne::Rtsne()’s quality. Random starts come seed argument, results identical number cpus. New umap() runs uniform manifold approximation projection (UMAP) dist object, following uwot::umap() defaults: exact nearest neighbours, smooth-kNN calibration fuzzy union (identical uwot’s), spectral start normalized graph Laplacian, layout optimization uwot’s batch mode (batch = TRUE: per-epoch gradients, Adam), gives uwot’s coordinates start seeds. Every stage runs parallel C, neighbours straight dist triangle without n--n matrix. Random numbers come seed argument, results identical number cpus. min_dist defaults canonical 0.1 (umap-learn’s), uwot’s 0.01. New permanova() runs permutational multivariate analysis variance dist object sample metadata. Like ecodive’s tests, takes groups: one value per sample (categories numeric covariate), column name data. several variables, give data formula instead: factors, covariates, interactions, Condition() terms. gives table vegan::adonis2() (Df, sums squares, R2, F, p-values), testing model whole term sequentially, marginally, contrast, optional strata. Given permutation matrix, permuted F statistics p-values identical adonis2()’s. returns list class "ecodive_test", like mrpp(): model’s F, p-value, z-score (summary(vegan::permustats())) number permutations come first, whatever , R2 adonis2()’s table, table. sums squares come straight dist triangle, without n--n matrices adonis2() builds permutation, permutations run parallel. one thread 25 50 times faster adonis2() 200 samples, 100 300 times faster 1,000. Permutations come seed argument, results identical number cpus. Like adonis2(), also takes distances left-hand side formula: permanova(dm ~ treatment + ph, data). New mrpp() runs multi-response permutation procedure dist object sample’s group, vegan::mrpp(): observed expected weighted mean within-group distance (delta), chance-corrected within-group agreement , group’s mean distance, permutation p-value, group weights 'n', 'n-1' 'n(n-1)' (vegan’s weight.type 1 3) optional strata. also gives standardized effect size z summary(vegan::permustats()). Given permutation matrix, permuted deltas, p-values z vegan::mrpp(). permutation costs one comparison per pair samples, read straight dist triangle; 500 samples 999 permutations 60 times faster vegan::mrpp() one thread. Results identical number cpus. Like ecodive’s permutation tests, returns list class "ecodive_test" whose statistic, p_value, z n_perm come first, .data.frame() turns one row columns every test. New anosim() runs analysis similarities (ANOSIM) dist object sample’s group, given vector column sample metadata, optional strata. Given permutation matrix, R statistic, permuted R values p-value match vegan::anosim()’s. ranks distances , radix sort, permutation needs one pass ranks, without n--n matrices vegan::anosim() builds; permutations run parallel. 300 samples 999 permutations takes tenth second, seven vegan::anosim(). Results identical number cpus. New permdisp() tests homogeneity multivariate dispersions (PERMDISP), vegan::betadisper() followed vegan::permutest(): sample’s distance group’s centroid (default) spatial median, group’s mean distance, ANOVA F permutation p-value, plus optional pairwise t tests small-group bias adjustment. Distances centroids come distances within groups alone, eigendecomposition: match betadisper()’s rounding error, 100 times faster 1,000 samples. betadisper() defaults spatial medians instead: pass type = "median" compare . permdisp() solves exactly, betadisper()’s optimizer stops 1e-5. Given permutation matrix, p-values identical permutest()’s. Permutations come seed argument, can restricted strata, results identical number cpus. New mantel() runs Mantel test correlation two distance matrices (Pearson, Spearman, Kendall), new mantel_partial() partial Mantel test, removes effect third (given). give statistics vegan::mantel() vegan::mantel.partial(), , given permutation matrix, permuted statistics p-values. second third matrices may also numeric vectors, one value per sample (age), samples matched name. add lower-tail two-sided tests (alternative). permutation one pass dist triangle, n--n matrix (Kendall’s tau-b Knight’s merge sort rather cor()’s quadratic count), permutations run parallel. Permutations come seed argument, results identical number cpus. New dist_test(dm, test, groups, data, ...) runs tests name, dist_ord() ordination methods: dist_test(dm, "mrpp", "treatment", meta) mrpp(dm, "treatment", meta), arguments (mantel()’s method) pass . checks variable kind test takes: categorical groups anosim, mrpp permdisp, numeric values mantel mantel_partial (passed y), either permanova. list_dist_tests() match_dist_test() list look tests, forgiving name matching ("adonis2" finds permanova, "betadisper" finds permdisp). permanova(), anosim(), mrpp() permdisp() take pairwise = TRUE also compare pair groups, usual overall test across several groups, p_adjust adjust pairs’ p-values multiple testing: stats::p.adjust.methods, Holm’s method default. permanova(), anosim() mrpp() rerun test pair’s samples, q2-diversity’s beta_group_significance(pairwise=True) pairwiseAdonis’s pairwise.adonis2() , pair’s statistics, z-score, sample size, raw adjusted p-values pairwise data frame. Given permutations, pairs’ statistics p-values identical vegan’s tests pair. pair’s random permutations come seed pair, results identical number cpus; supplied permutations matrix cut pair’s samples. pair can’t tested, two groups one sample, gives NAs warning. permdisp()’s pairwise t tests gain p_adjusted p_adjusted_perm (p-value columns adjusted across pairs, vegan::permutest() doesn’t ), z, n n_perm columns, pairwise table now columns . One rule aligns every per-sample argument (groups, strata, Mantel tests’ y given) permanova(), mrpp(), anosim(), permdisp(), mantel(), mantel_partial(), envfit() dist_test(): data, column name one value per row data; without , one value per sample, matched name named, else position. checks messages apply everywhere. vegan::adonis2(), permanova() needs groups formula (use formula = ~ . test every column data). permutations limited 1e8. New dbrda() runs distance-based redundancy analysis (db-RDA): axes dist object sample metadata explain, given formula ~ treatment + Condition(site). gives eigenvalues, inertia, site scores, biplot scores centroids vegan::dbrda() (axis’s sign; vegan::capscale(), differs non-Euclidean distances), without forming n--n matrix: constrained axes come small eigenproblem, unconstrained axes (MDS1, …) computed constraints give fewer n_axes axes. results identical number cpus. vegan, dbrda(dm ~ treatment, data) works , formula Condition() terms gives unconstrained ordination removing effect. dbrda() takes groups, data formula permanova(): one variable groups (vector column data), data formula, dm ~ terms, dist_ord(dm, "dbrda", "treatment", meta) works. results gain r_squared adj_r_squared, vegan::RsquareAdj(), including partial models. New capscale() runs constrained analysis principal coordinates. gives results vegan::capscale() (phyloseq::ordinate(method = "CAP")), imaginary inertia negative eigenvalues reported inertia. Euclidean distances take dbrda()’s fast path; otherwise threaded eigendecomposition makes five times faster vegan::capscale() one thread. Also available dist_ord(dm, "capscale", ...). New rda() runs redundancy analysis count table: axes (normalized) table sample metadata explain (RDA1, …), principal components rest (PC1, …). norm = 'hellinger' 'chord' gives transformation-based RDA (tb-RDA), Condition() terms partial RDA. takes groups, data formula dbrda() (counts ~ terms, vegan::rda()), model PCA. gives site scores, species scores (loadings), eigenvalues, inertia, R-squared, biplot scores centroids vegan::rda() (axis’s sign), sharing dbrda()’s solver pca()’s sparse table products, table never made dense: 3,000 samples 2,000 taxa takes half second vegan::rda() takes minute. Results identical number cpus. Also available count_ord(counts, "rda", ...). permutation test permanova() Euclidean distances normalized table. New cca() runs canonical correspondence analysis (ter Braak 1986) table abundances: correspondence analysis axes, chi-square metric, sample metadata explain (CCA1, …), correspondence analysis axes rest (CA1, …). takes groups, data formula rda() , including Condition() partial CCA counts ~ terms, model correspondence analysis. gives site scores, species scores (loadings), eigenvalues, inertia, R-squared, biplot scores centroids vegan::cca() (axis’s sign), permutation-based adjusted R-squared vegan::RsquareAdj() permutations (permutations seed), partial CCA included. shares rda()’s solver, chi-square weights, multiplies table’s non-zero values , sparse table never made dense: 3,000 samples 2,000 taxa takes half second vegan::cca() takes minute. Results identical number cpus. Also available count_ord(counts, "cca", ...). New ca() runs correspondence analysis table abundances: unconstrained ordination chi-square metric, species scores (loadings). gives site scores, species scores, eigenvalues inertia vegan::ca() (vegan::cca() without constraints), ade4::dudi.coa() scikit-bio’s ca() (axis’s sign), cca() model, whose sparse solver shares. Results identical number cpus. Also available count_ord(counts, "ca"); "CA" selects , dist_ord(dm, "ca") points count_ord(). New envfit() fits sample metadata (data) feature tables (counts, taxa abundances) onto ordination, biplots: arrow r-squared numeric variable feature, centroid factor level, permutation p-values. gives arrows, r-squared centroids vegan::envfit(), p-values permutation matrix. permutation costs multiply-adds per non-zero value table, refitting, sparse tables never made dense, thousands taxa 999 permutations take well second (minutes vegan). fits every axis ordination default (vegan fits first two), results identical number cpus. New procrustes() rotates, reflects, optionally dilates one ordination fit another samples, reports Procrustes sum squares, m^2: similar, say, Bray-Curtis UniFrac PCoAs (16S metagenomic ones) samples . gives rotation, translation, dilation, residuals m^2 vegan::procrustes() (symmetric m^2 SciPy’s scipy.spatial.procrustes()), takes arguments procrustes(ord, target): vegan::procrustes(target, ord). vegan’s scale called dilate. Inputs may dist objects, ordinated pcoa() first (n_axes axes), samples matched name. result rotated ordination, rest attributes. New procrustes_test() runs Procrustes randomization test (PROTEST), giving statistic vegan::protest() p-values permutation matrix, parallel C, strata, identical results number cpus. New plsda() runs partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA): components count table best separate known groups, PLS regression dummy matrix groups (ported scikit-learn’s PLSRegression). gives scores, weights, loadings Y loadings scikit-learn, scores, explained variance VIP mixOmics::plsda() (component’s sign), also returns feature’s VIP group’s centroid. component’s weights computed directly rather NIPALS iteration, don’t depend convergence tolerance. takes groups data permanova() , every norm ('clr' usual choice microbiome counts), sparse tables, never makes dense: 1,000 samples 5,000 taxa take tenth second, mixOmics::plsda() takes second. Results identical number cpus. count_ord(counts, 'plsda', groups) runs . Like every supervised method, separates groups given, validate separation (e.g. permanova()). New oplsda() runs orthogonal PLS discriminant analysis (OPLS-DA) two groups: one predictive component (p1) separates orthogonal components (o1, o2, …) rest table’s variation (ported pyopls). gives orthogonal scores, weights loadings pyopls, scores, loadings, weights, R2X, R2Y VIP ropls::opls() (component’s sign), also returns group’s centroid. takes groups, data, every norm every table type plsda() , never makes sparse table dense: 1,000 samples, 5,000 taxa two orthogonal components take tenth second, ropls::opls() takes 8 (including cross-validation). Results identical number cpus. count_ord(counts, 'oplsda', groups) runs . two groups, use plsda(). New lda() runs linear discriminant analysis (Fisher’s discriminant axes, ported scikit-learn’s LinearDiscriminantAnalysis "svd" solver). gives scores, coefficients (scaling), group means proportion trace MASS::lda() predict() (axis’s sign), optional prior probabilities, scores scikit-learn constant factor (scikit-learn divides within-group covariance n, n - g). takes groups data plsda() , every norm every table type, stops error within-group covariance singular, microbiome tables taxa samples: run PCoA PCA axes instead. 5,000 samples 200 features take 0.2 seconds, MASS::lda() takes 0.8. Results identical number cpus. count_ord(counts, 'lda', groups) runs . Ordinations many axes faster several threads. block Lanczos solver behind pcoa(), pca(), dbrda(), capscale(), rda(), cca(), rpca() umap()’s spectral start now splits steps basis (products small matrices, dot products , four axes, block Gram-Schmidt) among cpus, far work worth , well products data. 4 threads, pcoa() 50 axes takes 1.4 s instead 2.5 1,000 samples 15 s instead 27 5,000, dbrda() 40 axes 2,000 samples 3.3 s instead 5.6. Results stay identical number cpus; four axes unchanged, differ rounding. New capda() runs Anderson & Willis’s (2003) discriminant canonical analysis principal coordinates (CAP, PRIMER-PERMANOVA+): lda() first m axes pcoa(), distances, m chosen leave-one-classification success (max_pcoa_axes, 50 default; ties, smallest m), permutation test trace statistic (sum squared canonical correlations), strata supplied permutation matrix. gives m, classification success, leave-one-classes, squared canonical correlations scores BiodiversityR::CAPdiscrim(), whose leave-one-posteriors underflow samples far every group, stops group one sample (capda() counts samples misclassified). success every m considered leave-one-table returned. Results identical number cpus. dist_ord(dm, 'capda', groups) runs ; 'CAP' still selects capscale(), db-RDA. lda()’s error singular within-group covariance now suggests capda(). New simper() runs similarity percentages analysis (SIMPER): breaks mean Bray-Curtis dissimilarity pair groups taxon’s contribution, sd, ratio, groups’ mean abundances cumulative proportion, following ecopy’s simper(), gives taxon permutation p-value (Clarke 1993), adjusted within pair p_adjust (Holm’s method default). gives results vegan::simper() summary() , one data frame. p-values count permuted contributions least large observed one, Clarke (1993) ; vegan counts larger ones, makes p-values small small groups. pairwise tests, pair’s permutations shuffle samples (vegan shuffles ). takes groups data permanova() , strata, norm ('none' default, vegan) sparse tables, never makes dense, runs parallel C: 300 samples 3,000 taxa, three pairs 99 permutations, take 2 seconds one thread, vegan::simper() takes 27 seconds one pair. Results identical number cpus. docs explain SIMPER’s ranking mixes differences mean variability (Warton et al. 2012). New bioenv() finds subset environmental variables whose distances among samples best match community distances (BIOENV; Clarke & Ainsworth 1993): subset size, subset highest rank correlation dm, one data frame, best subset overall attribute best. follows scikit-bio’s bioenv() gives subsets correlations vegan::bioenv(), vegan’s options: method (Spearman, Pearson Kendall), metric ('euclidean', 'mahalanobis', 'manhattan' 'gower'), max_vars (vegan’s upto) given (vegan’s partial, also Kendall, vegan refuses). Variables come data, formula numeric columns, samples matched name. Every subset searched parallel C, n--n matrix: 100 samples 12 variables (4,095 subsets) take 1.2 seconds one thread, vegan::bioenv() takes 5.5. Results identical number cpus. New varpart() partitions variation community among two four sets explanatory variables (Borcard et al. 1992): fractions set explains , share, residuals, adjusted R-squared (partial) RDAs count table (norm, "hellinger"), db-RDAs dist, , chisquare = TRUE, CCAs permutation-estimated adjusted R-squared (Peres-Neto et al. 2006). gives fractions vegan::varpart() two, three four sets, one data frame named vegan’s letters ([], [b], …), vegan’s union conditional fractions attributes text Venn diagram printed. set formula data, data frame, matrix, vector, matched samples name. RDA db-RDA, one pass data gives every union’s R-squared, n--n matrix sparse tables kept sparse: 3,000 samples, 2,000 taxa (5% non-zero) three sets, takes 0.13 seconds 4 threads (Hellinger table Bray-Curtis distances), vegan::varpart() takes 3.5. Results identical number cpus. New forward_select() picks explanatory variables one time adjusted R-squared, permutation test added variable Blanchet et al.’s (2008) double stopping rule, RDA count table (norm) db-RDA dist. selects variables order vegan::ordiR2step(), adjusted R-squared F, p-values given permutations. Candidates terms formula data (factors enter whole, interactions main effects, Condition() terms covariables). default first tests global model selects nothing significant; max_vars caps number variables, strata restricts permutations. Every candidate’s adjusted R-squared comes one pass data, chosen candidate step tested: 1,000 samples, 500 taxa, 11 candidates 199 permutations, takes 0.17 seconds 4 threads Hellinger table 0.08 Bray-Curtis distances, vegan::ordiR2step() takes 58 85. Results identical number cpus. New alr() ilr(), additive isometric log-ratio transforms, complete clr rclr norm already offers. alr() divides denominator feature choose (default: scikit-bio uses first feature compositions last). ilr() takes Helmert basis scikit-bio uses default, sequential binary partition (converted scikit-bio’s sbp_basis()), orthonormal basis, matched features name. give coordinates scikit-bio’s alr() ilr() (alr() last bit, ilr() 1e-15), take every table type zeros handled shared pseudocount rule, return dense matrix input’s orientation method, denominator basis, pseudocount attributes, ready pca(), rda(), lda() envfit(). default basis applied running sum, without dense product: 2,000 samples 5,000 taxa take 0.2 seconds, normalize(x, 'clr') %*% t(basis) takes 30 R’s reference BLAS. Euclidean distances ilr() coordinates aitchison() distances, basis. Results identical number cpus. New replace_zeros() replaces zeros count table small positive values, log ratios (norm = 'clr', aitchison(), alr(), ilr()) can taken without pseudocount: result zeros, use none give warning. runs zero replacement method name, count_ord() ordinations, list_zero_replacements() match_zero_replacement() list look methods. first replace_zeros_mult(), multiplicative replacement (Martín-Fernández et al. 2003): every zero becomes delta (one value, one per sample; scikit-bio’s 1 / D^2 default) sample’s non-zero proportions shrink factor, keeping ratios. results bit-identical scikit-bio’s multi_replace(). Every method returns dense matrix proportions input’s orientation, method, parameters n_replaced attributes, takes every table type: sparse 2,000 5,000 table takes 0.2 seconds. New log_ratio() balance() give one log ratio per sample numerator denominator group features (names, indices logical vectors), named vector drops straight metadata test. log_ratio() log ratio summed abundances, Qurro plots (identical Qurro’s qarcoal()); needs pseudocount default, gives NA, one warning, sum balance() isometric log-ratio balance, scaled log ratio geometric means: bit-identical matching coordinate ilr() sequential binary partition, equal scikit-bio’s 6e-16, without building full basis; zeros follow shared pseudocount rule whole table, output replace_zeros() needs none. take every table type keep sparse tables sparse: 2,000 samples 5,000 taxa take 0.1 seconds. Qurro-style rank plots log ratios (Fedarko et al. 2020; Morton et al. 2019’s reference frames): plot(fit, type = "rank") draws every feature bar effect, sorted, results dirmult_ttest(), ancombc(), ancombc2(), da_ttest(), da_wilcoxon(), da_lm() linda(), plot(ord, type = "rank") loadings one axis pca(), rpca(), rpca_phylo(), rda() ordinations loadings. numerator denominator highlight log ratio’s features. plot(ord, type = "n") types still reach plot.default(). New log_ratio_features(x, n) picks n top- bottom-ranked features result (Qurro’s “autoselection”), numerator denominator log_ratio() balance(). selects features Qurro 0.9.0’s code every reference case, ties included, log_ratio() matches Qurro’s qarcoal() within one rounding log(). log_ratio() balance() results class ecodive_log_ratio, short print() plot(): samples’ values group (box plot samples , spread without random number generator), numeric variable, together, leaving counting undefined values. stay numeric vectors everywhere else; subsetting, sort() arithmetic return plain named vectors. New vlr(), rho_p() phi_s() measure proportionality every pair features, compositionally valid alternative correlating relative abundances (Lovell et al. 2015). vlr() variance log ratio, equal scikit-bio’s pairwise_vlr() 4e-15 computed differences rather covariance matrix, nearly proportional pairs keep precision. rho_p() Erb & Notredame’s proportionality correlation (propr’s "rho") phi_s() symmetric phi Quinn et al. (propr’s "phs"), clr default denominator (one feature, alr, set). returns dist features, ready pcoa() hclust() (rho_p(), similarity, thresholding). take every table type keep sparse, run parallel, give identical results cpus: 4.5 million pairs 3,000 taxa 500 samples take second 4 cores. New sparcc() estimates correlations taxa’s log absolute abundances relative abundances SparCC (Friedman & Alm 2012), co-occurrence networks often reported microbiome data: Dirichlet draws sample’s fractions (zeros need pseudocount), basis variances SparCC’s sparsity assumption, iterative exclusion strongly correlated pairs, pair’s median draws. settings agrees FastSpar SpiecEasi within noise random draws (0.002 counts thousands). permutations adds FastSpar’s p-values (resampled null datasets; never 0), parallel triangle. Like rho_p(), returns dist features, plot() draws diverging scale clust clusters 1 - r. title: ecodive 2.3.2
text: Fixed aitchison(), every beta metric called norm = 'clr', returning NaN (, chebyshev(), wrong values) every sample pair. Two bugs involved: Data zeros (pseudocount 0) hit log(0) * 0, NaN. pseudocount truncated integer C, values 1, including automatic min(counts[counts > 0]) / 2, became 0, values like 1.5 silently rounded . gower() norm = 'clr' now computes feature’s range, distance features absent samples, feature’s CLR values instead treating absent features 0. gower() negative inputs (e.g. norm = 'rclr') now also uses full min--max range.

title: ecodive 2.3.1
text: CRAN release: 2026-11-05 read_tree() now handles quoted labels per Newick standard: '' inside quoted label decoded one literal apostrophe, '''s' read . Square brackets inside quotes literal characters rather comments, labels like 'o__[Saprospirales]' longer truncated. Newlines whitespace inside quotes preserved. Comments ([...]) outside quotes may contain apostrophes. read_tree() raises informative error, position problem, malformed input unclosed quote, comment, parenthesis. Previously return garbled tree. read_tree()’s parser now linear-time non-recursive, making 4x faster typical 100,000-tip tree much faster deep trees.
